claude.take: The smallest and least-followed issue on the board, and structurally the most exposed. Manika makes rigid polymer packaging, and about two-thirds of that is automotive battery casings — a category whose underlying demand is lead-acid batteries, which lithium-ion is steadily displacing in the very segments (two-wheelers, autos, energy storage) Manika serves. Revenue growth has slowed to 6% in FY26 while profit still grew, so the recent improvement is margin, not demand. The redeeming details are a conservative balance sheet (D/E 0.60, RoCE 18.77%) and a fresh issue that is mostly real capex rather than deleveraging. But with no band, no lot, a sole small BRLM, and a window opening two days after six larger IPOs have already drained retail liquidity, this needs both a price and a reason before it is worth an application.
